title: Hosting choice vignette - finserv decision aid
content:
Context: small-to-mid fintech customer (EU data residency requirement) wants a 6-week POC to validate transaction summarization + fraud-signal enrichment at scale. Primary success criteria: p99 latency <= 120ms for inference path, end-to-end throughput 50-200 QPS (bursty), acceptable monthly infra cost < $8k for prototype, and no customer data leaving EU region. Secondary: model quality within +-3% of baseline rouge/recall metrics and ability to switch to private deployment for production without rewrites.

Purpose of this vignette: provide a compact, decision-oriented comparison (hosted / dedicated / private), a recommended phased plan for the POC, mitigation options for the main risks we typically hit in regulated finserv pilots, and an actionable workshop agenda to align stakeholders. This is intentionally concise — use as a prep doc for the kickoff.

Customer constraints and signals (collected pre-kickoff):
- Data residency: EU-only (must hold raw transactions in EU).
- Compliance appetite: wants SOC2 + contractual DPIA; not ready for full on-premair-gapped setup during POC.
- Traffic pattern: 30 min bursts during batch runs; regular background queries at 10-20 QPS.
- Latency SLO: p99 <= 120ms for the model inference step (excluding heavy enrichment joins).
- Ops maturity: small infra team; they prefer managed for first 90 days.

Quick comparison (one-liners):
- Hosted: fastest to stand up, minimal ops, best for iterating prompts and model variants, but needs careful region control and contractual assurances for PII handling; cost can be higher at scale unless we tune batching and cache aggressively.
- Dedicated: predictable throughput and SLA-backed latency; good mid-term option for predictable cost; requires capacity sizing and some customer coordination for burst handling.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): strongest control, data residency guarantees, meets strict compliance; highest ops overhead and longest lead time — not ideal to start POC unless customer has existing infra and a long procurement runway.

Decision matrix (criteria -> impact / recommended pick):
- Time-to-first-query: Hosted (best) > Dedicated > Private (slowest)
- Data residency/compliance: Private (best) > Dedicated (good if Dedicated in EU) > Hosted (depends on provider region + contract)
- Latency predictability at target load: Dedicated (best) > Private (if collocated) > Hosted (depends on noisy neighbors)
- Operational overhead (customer): Hosted (low) > Dedicated (medium) > Private (high)
- Cost predictability: Dedicated (best) > Private (if amortized) > Hosted (variable but can be optimized)

Recommendation (short): start the POC on EU-hosted (hosted mode) with a parallel small dedicated replica for latency-sensitive canary tests. Rationale: hosted gives fastest feedback for prompts and model selection; a dedicated replica validates latency SLAs under real load and serves as the migration target if we need to move to reserved capacity for cost predictability. Private only if procurement and infra readiness align before production readiness (not as POC default).

Phased plan (6 weeks):
- Week 0 (pre-kickoff): finalize contracts (EU data residency addendum), sign quick NDA, set up team channels. Tickets: JIRA-SE-8421 (POC brief), CONFLUENCE-SE-FIN-POC (shared doc). Owner: Solutions SE.
- Week 1 (kickoff + baseline): deploy hosted instance in EU region, seed sample dataset (anonymized), run baseline model tests. Deliverable: baseline perf report (latency, quality).
- Week 2 (iteration): prompt engineering, local caching layer experiment, measure token cost. Deliverable: prompt iteration log and cost projection.
- Week 3 (scale test): spin up small dedicated pool (reserved GPUs in EU) and replay a traffic burst; compare p99 and tail latencies. Deliverable: dedicated vs hosted latency delta.
- Week 4 (security & compliance check): run audit checklist, verify KMS integration for hosted keys or dedicated key management. Deliverable: compliance shortlist and DPIA draft.
- Week 5 (canary flows + fallbacks): route 10-20% traffic to dedicated replica for latency-sensitive endpoints, validate failover to hosted or a smaller model variant under simulated outage.
- Week 6 (wrap + recommendation): produce final POC report and recommended production pathway (hosted->dedicated or private lift-and-shift).

Technical knobs to run during POC (practical experiments):
- Batching config sweep (latency vs cost) using realistic request arrival traces.
- KV/prefix caching for repeated context (savings on warm-start tokens).
- Quantized model evaluation (FP16 vs int8) to confirm quality tradeoff under compute-constrained dedicated pools.
- Autoscaling thresholds and burst capacity test for dedicated pool (to validate SLA under sudden bursts).
- Function/tool calling tests if downstream enrichment services are synchronous (measure E2E tail).

Risk log (top 6) + mitigations:
1) Data residency contract gap -> mitigation: sign EU-data addendum and keep raw data in customer-controlled S3 bucket; use hosted private link to inference.
2) Tail latency spikes on hosted -> mitigation: dedicated replica for critical routes, set automatic fallback to smaller model + cached responses.
3) Procurement delays for dedicated -> mitigation: pre-buy minimal burst capacity as hosted reserved credits; plan dedicated trial only for week 3.
4) Model quality regression after quantization -> mitigation: maintain pre-quant eval set and run automated regressions; gate any quantized rollout on quality thresholds.
5) Cost overrun from excessive sampling -> mitigation: token caps, rate limit, sampling budget for experimentation, and cost dashboards instrumented in week 1.
6) Customer ops bandwidth too low -> mitigation: Redwood-managed runbook for first 90 days + weekly handoff calls.

Workshop agenda (90 minutes) — goal: align on success metrics, constraints, and immediate actions
- 0–10m: Introductions and POC objectives (owner: Customer TPM)
- 10–25m: Architecture primer (hosted/dedicated/private) and decision tradeoffs (owner: Solutions SE)
- 25–45m: Traffic and latency profile validation (engineer: Customer infra + Redwood SRE)
- 45–60m: Compliance checklist review (security: Customer compliance + Redwood security)
- 60–80m: Runbook & escalation paths; failover policy (owner: Solutions SE)
- 80–90m: Action items and immediate next steps (capture owners + due dates)

Open questions to resolve in kickoff:
- Is the customer willing to accept a hosted EU region with contractual DPIA addendum for the POC, or must raw data remain in their VPC from day 1?
- Do they have a preferred KMS provider we must integrate with for encryption-at-rest?
- Expected concurrency at peak (exact numbers) and cost tolerance if we need 2x baseline GPU in dedicated for burst windows.

Decision triggers to move from hosted -> dedicated -> private:
- Hosted->Dedicated: if p99 on hosted exceeds 120ms under replayed production-like traffic and cost savings justify reserved capacity.
- Dedicated->Private: if contractual / audit requirements mandate private control of keys, or if network egress policies block hosted options.

Actionable checklist (owners):
- Confirm EU-data addendum signed (Owner: Solutions AE) — JIRA-SE-8421-1
- Provision hosted EU instance + instrument cost & latency dashboards (Owner: Redwood infra eng) — JIRA-SE-8421-2
- Create small dedicated pool in EU for week 3 (Owner: Redwood capacity ops) — JIRA-SE-8421-3
- Prepare compliance checklist & DPIA draft (Owner: Customer compliance + Redwood security) — JIRA-SE-8421-4
- Run quantization smoke tests on dev data (Owner: Applied ML) — JIRA-SE-8421-5

Notes to self / SE talking points: keep language simple when describing "dedicated" vs "private" — use "reserved capacity" and "customer-managed VPC" wording. Emphasize that the POC's goal is decision-making (which hosting to pick) not premature production hardening. Highlight rollback options and cost caps early to reduce procurement friction.

Appendix (quick templates):
- Canary rollout percentages: 5% -> 20% -> 50% over 48 hour windows with abort criteria tied to p99 and error rate thresholds.
- Suggested SLOs to negotiate: p50 <= 40ms, p90 <= 80ms, p99 <= 120ms for model inference.
- Minimal telemetry: token counts, per-request latency histogram, model variant tag, cache hit rate, GPU utilization (for dedicated), and cost per 1k requests.

End of vignette — this doc is a working draft for the kickoff. Use it to steer the discussion and create JIRA tasks after the meeting.

Revision history: 2024-11-18 initial draft by LP; 2024-12-05 added dedicated pool experiment notes (DM); 2025-01-14 updated recommendation after capacity ops input (Owen).
